issues.legal_issue: A party’s possession of disputed land, without a legal right to it, does not by itself establish that the party was the aggressor in a violent incident over the land.
material_facts: Revenue records showed that the accused party had cultivated and harvested crops on the land before the incident, although its possession was recorded as forcible and without legal right.
A prosecution witness admitted that the accused party had harvested a crop, while the prosecution also claimed that its side had obtained rights to the land and constructed a dera there.
A civil suit concerning possession was pending, and the evidence showed continuing disputes between the two sides over possession.
issues.conclusion: The evidence did not support the inference that the accused party was the aggressor merely because of the disputed possession of the land.
issues.legal_principle: Actual possession is relevant even when it is without legal right. In a criminal case arising from a dispute over land, the absence of legal title does not establish that the party in possession came to disturb another party’s possession; possession alone could not support the aggressor finding here. No earlier cases or statutory provisions were relied on for this principle.

predicates.violent_criminal_case_over_disputed_land: A criminal case concerns violence arising from a dispute over possession of land.
predicates.possession_evidence_favors_accused_party: Records or admissions indicate that the accused side was in actual possession of the land, even if that possession was without legal right.
predicates.competing_possession_claims: The parties asserted competing claims to possession of the land.

issues.definition: When a violent criminal case arises from disputed land possession, the evidence favors the accused side’s actual possession, and both sides claim possession, the accused side is not proved to be the aggressor on possession alone.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for murder or attempted murder cannot stand when the prosecution evidence does not reliably establish that the accused side initiated the violence and the account of the incident is materially inconsistent with the injury evidence.
material_facts: The prosecution relied on three eyewitnesses, whose account the High Court itself found to contain material improbabilities.
The prosecution side sustained seven injuries, while five members of the accused side sustained 57 injuries; two of those five were severely beaten, and one later died from the injuries.

The prosecution account was that the accused side killed one person and injured another at the outset, after which three people on the prosecution side inflicted the many injuries on five armed members of the accused side without themselves receiving a scratch.

The appellant was convicted of murder under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code and attempted murder under Section 307 read with Section 34; the Supreme Court found that the use of guns by the accused side did not, by itself, establish that it was the aggressor or guilty of those offences.
issues.conclusion: The appellant’s guilt was not proved beyond reasonable doubt; the appeal was allowed and the conviction and sentences were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The prosecution must establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt. The Court assessed the charges under Sections 302 and 307 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code against the reliability of the eyewitness account and the injuries on both sides. Use of a gun alone did not establish that the accused were aggressors or guilty of murder or attempted murder. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.eyewitness_account_materially_improbable: The prosecution’s eyewitness account contains material improbabilities about how the incident occurred.
predicates.injury_pattern_inconsistent_with_prosecu: The number or severity of injuries on the accused side is inconsistent with the prosecution’s account of the incident.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal from conviction, if material improbabilities in the eyewitness account and the injury pattern undermine the prosecution’s version, the conviction is set aside because guilt is not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
